This article is a test fixture. It does not represent Miguel’s opinions or describe a real project. **The production build must not include the fixture collections.**

## Start with a question

Good notes make a line of thinking visible. The point is to record the context, the choices, and what changed after trying something. A comfortable line length makes this easier to read on a large screen and on a phone.

> A note can be useful before it becomes a conclusion.

### Keep the details nearby

1. Describe the starting point.
2. Write down the constraints.
3. Explain the decision and what it taught you.

## Make the experiment small

The code block below tests horizontal scrolling without forcing the rest of the page off-screen.

```typescript
const extraordinarilyLongExampleForOverflowTesting =
  "This intentionally long line checks that the article remains within the viewport while the code block scrolls independently.";
console.log(extraordinarilyLongExampleForOverflowTesting);
```

| Choice         | Why it matters                    | What to verify             |
| -------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| Plain HTML     | Reading works without scripting   | Keyboard navigation        |
| Small scripts  | Interaction is an enhancement     | Search errors and recovery |
| Static content | Every article has its own address | Direct page loads          |

## Leave a useful record

Include links to the relevant project and enough detail for another person to follow the work. This English entry contains the unique search term **orbitalwalrus**.
